newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, CPO lower.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, CPO lower.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading on Thursday, with a holiday in Malaysia keeping the market lethargic, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,450-55 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at 1,440-45 rupiah.

The traders said crude palm oil was done at 1,271 rupiah/kg at a 500-tonne tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan, compared with the previous tender price of 1,279 rupiah. Another 500-tonne tender was called off despite a top bid of 1,271 rupiah/kg because it was below the seller's expectations.

"The market was not active due to the Labour Day holiday in Malaysia," one trader said. But another trader said there was some buying by players who had been keeping stocks low due to the ongoing general election campaign that began last Sunday.
"Some were coming back to the market after only buying oil that was just sufficient for their immediate needs," the trader said. "But today, their purchases were better."

The traders said sharp gains in Chicago soyoil futures overnight did not have any significant impact on the market. The rise was sparked by Sparks Companies executive Willard Sparks who forecast a rise in soybean futures.
